parts.text: Which claim explains why the assembly forms a regular hexagon?

options.text: Six congruent equilateral triangles fit around a common point because six $60^{\circ}$ angles sum to $360^{\circ}$, so the outer boundary has equal sides and equal $120^{\circ}$ angles.
The answer is the name regular hexagon, with no angle sum at the common point.
Any six triangles around a common point form a regular hexagon, even when the triangles are not congruent and not equilateral.
The same assembly also builds a regular pentagon from five such triangles around a common point.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Vikram cuts six congruent equilateral paper triangles and joins them at a common point to build a regular hexagon.

part_answers.answer: Six $60^{\circ}$ angles fill $360^{\circ}$ at the common point; congruent equilateral triangles give equal outer sides and $120^{\circ}$ hexagon angles.

teacher.key_rationale: Six 60° angles fill 360° at the centre; congruent equilateral triangles give equal outer sides and 120° angles. Naming regular hexagon alone substitutes a label. Dropping congruence/equilateral omits needed conditions. Extending the rule to a pentagon is out of scope.
